name: Cook a perfect omelet
blurb: The classic French omelette — pale yellow, no browning, softly set inside, rolled into a smooth cylinder — is a technical exercise that chefs still use as a hiring test.
gear: A well-seasoned or non-stick 20 cm pan
steps: Beat three eggs thoroughly with a pinch of salt until completely homogeneous — no streaks of white at all.
Melt butter over medium-low heat until it foams but does not colour. Heat control is the entire dish.
Pour in the eggs and stir constantly with the spatula while shaking the pan, making small curds.
When the eggs are about 80% set and still glossy, stop stirring and spread them evenly across the pan.
Tilt the pan away from you and roll the omelette over on itself, using the spatula to fold the far edge.
Turn out onto a plate seam-side down and brush with butter for shine. Eat immediately.
tips: Browning means the pan was too hot. A French omelette should have no colour whatsoever.
Overcooking is the only real failure. It carries on cooking on the plate, so pull it early.
Practise with three eggs a day for a week. Cheap homework.
proof: A pale, smooth, unbrowned omelette with a soft centre, rolled cleanly, three times running.
